sovereign_country.strategic_role: 全球跨境基金设立第一大国、超大型跨国投资架构

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Fast-Casual Self-Serve Broth Bowl Master Licensing

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law of 12 November 2004 on the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing, as amended (AML/CFT Law); Law of 13 January 2019 on the Register of Beneficial Owners (UBO Register Law); Law of 10 August 1915 on commercial companies, as amended; CSSF Circular 18/701; Grand-Ducal Regulation of 12 November 2004.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of passport of each UBO, director, and legal representative
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Public Security Bureau of the People's Republic of China passport office

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation of the Chinese corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR), People's Republic of China

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing or recent extract of the Chinese corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR), People's Republic of China

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of Attorney appointing the Luxembourg registered agent and domiciliation service
UBO declaration and corporate organisation chart identifying ultimate beneficial owner(s)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory pre-onboarding and ongoing screening of all UBOs, directors, managers, and authorized signatories against the EU consolidated financial sanctions list, UN Security Council sanctions committees, OFAC SDN list (where US dollar or US nexus exists), and the Luxembourg national embargo list. Politically Exposed Persons (PEPs) require enhanced due diligence and senior management approval in accordance with FATF Recommendations 10-12, CSSF Circular 18/701, and the AML/CFT Law. Continuous monitoring is required for the duration of the business relationship.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names may be expressed in French, German, or Luxembourgish; a non-Latin script name (e.g., Chinese characters) must be accompanied by a transliteration in Latin characters (pinyin) for RCS processing. The legal-form suffix must be in French: 'SCSp' or 'S.C.Sp.' appearing at the end of the name. All filings and accompanying communications must be in French, German, or Luxembourgish, with English or Chinese certified translations accepted only as supplementary evidence.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon name rejection, the applicant or legal counsel may file a reasoned administrative appeal with the RCSL within 15 days of the refusal. A further judicial review may be sought before the Tribunal de l'arrondissement de Luxembourg (Civil Division) within 30 days of the administrative decision. A one-time extension of the name reservation of 15 days is available if requested prior to expiry, but no additional extensions are granted. The appeal must address the specific rejection grounds, supply the proposed corrected name, and include evidence of compliance with the language and transliteration doctrine.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office is permissible for the SCSp only if an authorised domiciliation company under the Law of 31 May 1999 provides a formal registered office in Luxembourg and the entity maintains verifiable substance indicators. For a franchising licensing SCSp, the absence of employees or physical restaurant premises in Luxembourg is acceptable, provided the central administration, management decision-making, bank account signatory authority, and UBO directions are independently documented in Luxembourg. A virtual office without meaningful commercial activity will fail economic substance scrutiny under Luxembourg administrative practice.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: 15% annualized probability of an unannounced on-site inspection for the low-risk licensing entity; probability rises to 40% if the entity is domiciliated at a shared-office service centre with more than 40 registered entities, or upon adverse media or negative sanction screening results.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Company name availability check and reservation filing
SCSp partnership agreement drafting and notarisation (including notarial deed, if applicable)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market legal fee benchmark (six to eight hours at €250/hour)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: RCS registration and statutory publication in the Recueil des Sociétés et Associations (Memorial C)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory fee under the Grand-Ducal Regulation of 24 September 2013

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: UBO register filing and administrative processing
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory fee under the Law of 13 January 2019

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarisation and apostille of six Chinese corporate documents (passports, certificates, POA, UBO declaration)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Chinese notary public and Ministry of Foreign Affairs Apostille Office
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Regulated notarial fee schedule and apostille processing tariff at a fixed benchmark

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: AML/KYC and PEP screening of UBOs, directors, and legal representatives
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Registered compliance provider / external AML services firm
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Commercial provider benchmark for FATCA, OFAC, and EU sanctions screening package

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Certified translation of Chinese corporate source documents into French
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Certified translator on the Luxembourg Ministry of Justice approved list

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Tax and treaty advisory on SCSp pass-through classification and Luxembourg-China DTAA and BIT application

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as amended (the '1915 Law'), Articles 25-1 to 25-16 (Société en Commandite Spéciale – SCSp); Grand-Ducal Regulation on Company Registration
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés – RCS), operated by the Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) via the eJustice portal
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Limited Partnership Agreement (Contrat de Société) and RCS Registration Request (Requête d'immatriculation) filed electronically via eJustice
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital for an SCSp; capital contributions are freely determined in the partnership agreement and may be made in cash, in kind, or in industry. No escrow account is required under Luxembourg law for SCSp formation.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the subscriptions to the partnership interests of the SCSp as set out in the partnership agreement be and are hereby accepted, and the corresponding capital contributions be credited to the Company's accounts. RESOLVED, that the registered office of the SCSp be and is hereby fixed at [Address], Luxembourg, and that the general partner is authorized to execute the lease and register the principal place of business. RESOLVED, that [Name] be appointed as managing general partner (Gérant) and [Name] as compliance officer, each with the powers under the articles; and that the Gérant be authorized to make all filings with the RCS, tax and VAT authorities, and to take all steps required for licensing and opening bank accounts.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers – RCS (eJustice name reservation portal)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Perform a name availability search on the RCS database and file a name reservation request through the eJustice portal. The name must distinguish the entity and may include the abbreviation 'SCSp' or 'Special LP'. Provide the proposed name, corporate purpose, and confirming details of the general partner.
required_dossiers: Completed name reservation form
Copy of passport or national ID of the general partner
Proof of address of the general partner
Proposed list of names (at least three alternatives)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS rejects the name due to conflict or insufficient distinctiveness, file a revised reservation with an amended name within 5 business days; any queries are typically resolved via the eJustice message center.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and Execution of the Limited Partnership Agreement
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Civil law notary (only if real property contributions are foreseen) or directly among the partners
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Limited Partnership Agreement (LPA) in accordance with the 1915 Law, specifying the firm name, registered office, partners, capital contributions, profit sharing, management powers, and duration. Execute the LPA by private signature (unless notarization is required), with each partner signing in counterparts. Ensure the general partner provides a formal declaration of non-bankruptcy and legal capacity.
required_dossiers: Draft Limited Partnership Agreement
Identification documents of all partners (passport or national ID)
Declaration of non-bankruptcy of the general partner
Proof of registered office availability (letter of intent from landlord or owner)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary (when required) raises formal objections, adjust the LPA and resubmit for execution; if partners dispute terms, convene a meeting to resolve and restate the agreement.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of the Incorporation Dossier with the RCS
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) – Luxembourg District Court, via eJustice electronic filing
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the signed LPA, the completed registration request, and the required annexes to the RCS through the eJustice portal. Ensure all signatures are notarized or legalized if required, and pay the statutory filing fee electronically. The RCS reviews the dossier for conformity and issues the registration certificate (extrait d'immatriculation).
required_dossiers: Signed Limited Partnership Agreement
RCS registration request form
Passport copies of all partners
Declaration of non-bankruptcy of the general partner
Certified translation of the LPA if not in French, German, or English
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS issues a query or suspension notice, rectify the specified formal deficiencies and resubmit within 15 days; if the registration lapses, restart the process with a new filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication in the Official Electronic Gazette (RESA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: RCS (automatic publication) – Recueil Électronique des Sociétés et Associations (RESA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon successful registration, the RCS automatically transmits the statutory particulars for publication in the RESA online gazette. No separate action is required by the entity, but the entity must verify that the publication appears within the statutory time frame and retains the proof of publication for legal and banking purposes.
required_dossiers: RCS registration extract
Publication confirmation (if sought by the entity)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RESA publication is delayed or erroneous, contact the RCS to request republication or correction, supported by a copy of the registration extract.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Administration des Contributions Directes (ACD); Centre Commun de la Sécurité Sociale (CCSS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After obtaining the RCS extract, register with the ACD to obtain the national business number (matricule d'identification) and the corporate income tax file. If the entity will hire staff, also register as an employer with the CCSS and enroll in the employer social security plan. File the registration online via the MyGuichet.lu portal.
required_dossiers: RCS registration extract
Limited Partnership Agreement
Passport copies of the general partner and authorized signatories
Proof of registered office address
Declaration of commencement of activity (if applicable)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the ACD or CCSS queries the registration, provide additional documentation explaining the corporate purpose and ownership structure; deadlines may be extended by submitting a formal request.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: VAT Registration and Other Compliance Filings
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Administration de l'Enregistrement, des Domaines et de la TVA (AEDT)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the VAT registration application via the eCEC portal to obtain a Luxembourg VAT number for the SCSp. Indicate the planned restaurant activity (ISIC 5610) and anticipated turnover. If the entity will sell directly to consumers, the standard VAT rate applies; the application must be filed before the first taxable supply.
required_dossiers: RCS registration extract
ACD matricule certificate
Limited Partnership Agreement
Description of the activity and projected turnover
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the VAT registration is delayed or rejected, provide a detailed business plan and leasing contracts to substantiate the activity; where the AEDT requests further information, respond within the provided deadline and retain a copy of the submission.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of the Economy – General Directorate for Small and Medium-Sized Enterprises (Direction générale des PME), in consultation with the Luxembourg Chamber of Commerce (Chambre de Commerce)
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Autorisation d'établissement (Business Establishment Permit) under the Law of 2 September 2011 on the Access to the Professions; supplemented by a Food Service Operating Authorization issued by the Ministry of Health (Direction de la Santé) under Regulation (EC) 852/2004 on food hygiene

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Administration de l'Environnement (Environmental Administration), Luxembourg Ministry of Environment, Climate and Energy
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category B – Simplified environmental registration; full EIA not required for a small-scale fast-casual restaurant. An environmental self-assessment and registration notice must be submitted to the Administration de l'Environnement.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater discharge to the municipal sewer must conform to communal regulations and the Law of 19 December 2008 on Water Management; kitchen exhaust and odour emissions must meet IED/VOC thresholds for food service operations; waste oils and cooking residues must be disposed of via a licensed collector in accordance with the Waste Management Plan.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification from the Grand-Ducal Fire and Rescue Corps (Corps grand-ducal d'incendie et de secours – CGIDS) after local municipal inspection; structural load clearance from the municipal building inspectorate; occupational health and safety approval under the Labor Code (Code du travail), including an internal health and safety plan and medical surveillance for staff.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD) - Luxembourg Inland Revenue for direct taxes; Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) for VAT and registration duties; Administration des douanes et accises (ADA) for customs and export controls. Official portals: MyGuichet.lu for all filings, eCDF for electronic tax returns, and the RCS (Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés) for entity registration.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: Incorporate the SCSp by deed (notarial or private writing) in accordance with the Luxembourg law of 10 August 1915 on commercial companies, as amended, and register it with the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (RCS) to obtain the RCS number and the 13-digit entity matricule (national identification number). Non-resident general and limited partners must provide KYC/AML documentation and beneficial ownership declarations. Step 2: Register the SCSp for VAT with the AEDT using Form 10 (Déclaration d'assujettissement à la TVA), stating the commencement date of the franchising activity; the AEDT issues the 10-character LU VAT identification number. Step 3: If the SCSp has no Luxembourg commercial domicile or permanent establishment (PE), appoint a local VAT representative approved by the AEDT, who is jointly and severally liable for the VAT obligations. Step 4: Where a foreign partner becomes taxable in Luxembourg through a PE, file the ACD declaration of commencement within 15 days. Step 5: For the self-serve malatang fast-casual master franchise, no minimum capital is required, 100% non-resident ownership is permitted, and a food-service establishment licence (autorisation d'établissement) and municipal trade permit must be obtained before VAT-registered activity commences.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: The SCSp is fiscally transparent by default: income, gains, and net wealth are taxed directly at the level of the partners in proportion to their profit shares, with no Luxembourg corporate income tax (CIT), municipal business tax (UCT), or net wealth tax (NWT) at the entity level. The SCSp may make an irrevocable election under Article 157bis LIR (option pour l'assujettissement à l'impôt sur les sociétés) to be treated as a fully taxable entity for CIT, UCT, and NWT purposes, provided all partners are Luxembourg residents or residents of a treaty state; the election requires the written consent of all partners and registration in the RCS. Luxembourg does not operate a US-style check-the-box regime. Hybrid and reverse-hybrid mismatch rules (ATAD, transposed by the laws of 21 December 2018 and 20 December 2019) re-characterize the SCSp as taxable where the partner jurisdiction treats it as opaque (reverse-hybrid rule of Article 168ter LIR) and deny deductions for payments subject to hybrid mismatches.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.additional_note_residence_and_substance: For a fully foreign-owned SCSp without Luxembourg substance, the ACD may, under substance-over-form and abuse-of-law doctrines (Article 6 Abgabenordnung and Article 6 BStBl/LIR), challenge the Luxembourg tax residency of the entity or reclassify royalty payments where the central administration, statutory seat, or real management is not genuinely located in Luxembourg.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Taxe sur la valeur ajoutée - TVA), harmonized with EU Council Directive 2006/112/EC
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 35,000 - annual taxable turnover excluding VAT for the small-enterprise exemption (Article 57 LTVAT) applying only to EU-established taxable persons; non-established taxable persons have no threshold and must register from the first taxable transaction in Luxembourg (Articles 59-60 LTVAT).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: B2G e-invoicing has been mandatory since 2020 for invoices issued to Luxembourg public entities, submitted exclusively through the PEPPOL network (law of 16 May 2019 on electronic invoicing). There is no general B2B e-invoicing or real-time fiscal clearance/digital stamping mandate in Luxembourg as of the current stage; the EU ViDA package is expected to introduce mandatory B2B e-invoicing and transaction-based digital VAT reporting for Luxembourg taxable persons by 2030. VAT returns (Form 640) and EU recapitulative statements (Forms 641/642) must be filed electronically via MyGuichet.lu or eCDF, and all invoicing and export substantiation records must be retained for 10 years.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods: 0% VAT applies to exports of goods physically dispatched or transported outside the European Union by the supplier or on its behalf (Article 52(1) LTVAT), provided the buyer is a non-EU person, the goods leave the EU within 3 months of the supply (extendable to 12 months in justified cases), and the supplier holds full documentary proof of export. Services: master-franchise royalties, brand-licence fees, and self-serve concept know-how supplied B2B are outside Luxembourg VAT when the recipient is a taxable person established outside the EU (Article 58(1)(a) LTVAT), subject to written evidence of the recipient's VAT number or fiscal residence certificate, the royalty/service contract, and proof of payment. Where the non-EU recipient is a non-taxable person, the supply remains taxable in Luxembourg at 17% unless the service is physically performed abroad or directly related to exported goods (Article 52(b) LTVAT). Intra-EU B2B supplies of such services follow the reverse-charge mechanism, with the service taxable in the recipient's member state.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (SAD/DAU - Single Administrative Document) with the Movement Reference Number (MRN) and export acceptance printout from the Luxembourg ECS/AES customs system
Bill of Lading (B/L), CMR consignment note, or air waybill evidencing physical removal of the goods from the European Union
Proof of payment: SWIFT or inward remittance certificate evidencing receipt of export proceeds in foreign currency
Transport and delivery evidence: customs exit confirmation, warehouse receipts, or insurance documents corroborating the export movement
Royalty or master-franchise agreement identifying the non-EU franchisee, the precise service description, and the basis for the place-of-supply conclusion
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The AEDT and the Customs and Excise Administration (ADA) place the full documentary burden of proof on the SCSp; where export or offshore-service substantiation is incomplete or the physical EU-exit deadline is missed, zero-rating is retroactively reversed, the unpaid 17% VAT is clawed back, and default interest accrues at 0.6% per month on arrears. Administrative fines range from EUR 250 to EUR 25,000 per infraction under Articles 41-43 and 93 LTVAT. In cases of fraudulent, fictitious, or sham export structures, criminal prosecution may result in imprisonment of 8 days to 5 years and fines up to EUR 250,000; the general partner and the appointed Luxembourg VAT representative become jointly and severally liable; and the statute of limitations extends from 5 to 10 years. Serious violations can also lead to the suspension of the food-establishment licence and exclusion of the entity from the benefits of the small-enterprise exemption.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL) in coordination with the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF) for banking supervision and foreign exchange oversight.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Luxembourg, as a eurozone member, maintains full capital and current account convertibility under EU Treaty provisions on free movement of capital (TFEU Articles 63-66). Profit remittance and dividend distributions to non-resident partners are unrestricted, subject only to standard anti-money laundering verification and withholding tax formalities on non-cooperative jurisdictions. No prior administrative authorisation is required for FX operations or cross-border transfers; however, transactions involving sanctioned jurisdictions or cash-like instruments face augmented compliance screening.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Not applicable. Luxembourg imposes no statutory timeline or mandatory conversion ratio for export proceeds. Resident businesses may retain export receipts in any currency and maintain foreign-denominated accounts without obligation to convert to euro.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État (BCEE)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility: Medium to High for operational cash management, but Low for capital escrow. Luxembourg-regulated electronic money institutions (EMIs) and payment institutions (e.g., PayPal Luxembourg, Mangopay) can provide local IBANs and cross-border digital onboarding. Legal constraints: EMIs may not hold escrow accounts for regulated capital aggregation unless licensed under the Luxembourg law of 10 November 2009 on payment services and e-money, and they cannot act as deposit-taking institutions. The SCSp should maintain primary treasury accounts with a TLSB (fully licensed credit institution) and use an EMI only for ancillary FX payments and low-value royalty collections.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote onboarding is generally permitted for Luxembourg corporate entities provided the ultimate beneficial owner(s) undergo a video identification process acceptable to the bank under CSSF AML/CFT circulars (e.g., supervised remote onboarding using qualified trust services). Physical presence may be required by certain banks for high-risk or complex partnership structures, particularly when a non-European manager or general partner is involved. The SCSp must designate a resident agent or senior officer to attend an on-site interview if requested, to satisfy the ‘custody of identification data’ requirement.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: SCSp is a partnership with a non-resident general partner and opaque ownership layers
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete partnership agreement, register of partners, sub-structure diagram, UBO declarations for all natural persons owning ≥25% of the partnership, CVs of managers, and a notarised power of attorney to the Luxembourg bank signatory.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source of funds for capital injection exceeds €250,000 and originates from a China-based private investor
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Audited financial statements of the investing entity, evidence of corporate tax clearance and business registration from the State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR), source-of-wealth documentation for natural persons (tax assessment, bank statements, property contracts), and a certified copy of the foreign exchange registration certificate (FXIC) if required by the People's Bank of China for cross-border remittances.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Operational activity involves franchise royalty and trademark licensing from China
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Registered franchise agreement, trade mark registration certificates (EUIPO or WIPO), royalty calculation formula, and evidence of compliance with the EU Trade Secrets Directive; bank references from previous payment processors (e.g., Adyen, Stripe).

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unexplained cash withdrawals or high-frequency same-day payments in a fast-casual food franchise
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Detailed point-of-sale (POS) transaction logs, cash register Z-reports, inventory purchase invoices from approved suppliers, and a liquidity-flow forecast demonstrating operational consistency with daily cash turnover.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Capital injections for the SCSp must be executed via SWIFT MT103 for non-SEPA high-value transfers or SEPA Credit Transfer (SCT) for euro amounts up to €100,000. Purpose codes: for capital subscription from China, use the BOP code 'CE' (capital contributions) or 'PIE' (equity injections) under the ‘Payment – Capital’ category; the beneficiary reference must clearly state ‘SCSp capital under LSC law – not trade settlement’. The bank may request a board resolution, a joint signatory authorisation, and proof of the outbound FXIC (for Chinese remittances) to ensure compliance with both EU anti-money laundering and Chinese SAFE regulations.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Trade settlements for malatang ingredient and equipment imports from China should be settled via SWIFT MT103 documentation with attached invoices and contracts; for larger order quantities, useIrrevocable Documentary Letter of Credit (L/C) at sight, opened by the SCSp's Luxembourg bank and advised through a Chinese confirming bank. For intra-EU operational disbursements, SEPA Instant Credit Transfer (SCT Inst) is permissible up to €100,000, while payments beyond that threshold use the TARGET2 clearing system. High-frequency royalty remittances to the Chinese master licensor are best structured through a dedicated merchant account with an EMS (e.g., Paysera) using batch payments to minimise per-transaction costs, but must be mirrored in the audited partnership accounts.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright forward EUR/CNH contracts with settlement in euro (deliverable) for known, dated royalty and import payments, available from any Luxembourg credit institution without direct underlying trade evidence if within an ISDA/CEMA master agreement.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on CNY for hedging the residual RMB exposure from franchise royalties, permissible under Luxembourg law when manually settled in EUR based on a fixing rate (e.g., CNH fixing on WM/Refinitiv).

Currency swaps (FX swap/rolling spot) for converting euro inflows into RMB for Chinese supplier prepayments, authorised only when the counterparty is a EU-authorized bank or a MiFID II licensed investment firm.
Plain vanilla FX options (e.g., EUR/CNH calls) to cap future conversion costs without payment obligation, permitted for qualifying commercial hedging purposes under EMIR clearing thresholds.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual beneficial-ownership confirmation filing (RBE annual conformity declaration)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs (RBE), Luxembourg
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Once per calendar year, on or before 31 December; a change in shareholding or control triggers a separate filing within 30 days of such change
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative and criminal fines ranging from EUR 250 up to EUR 1,250,000 for legal persons, plus criminal liability of the gérant (Law of 13 January 2019; AML Law of 12 November 2004)

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Deposit of annual accounts with the business register (where the SCSp is not exempt from publication)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) via LBR, Luxembourg
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 7 months after the close of the fiscal year (31 July for a 31 December year-end)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Court-ordered civil fine of EUR 500–5,000 per defaulting manager; persistent non-compliance may lead to judicial dissolution and director disqualification

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Informative annual partnership tax return (transparent SCSp income-allocation declaration)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due by 31 December of the year following the tax year; extension typically granted to 31 March of year N+2 where a qualified tax adviser is mandated
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-payment interest of 0.6% per month; late-filing surcharge up to 10% of assessed partner tax; ex-officio assessment by the AED for non-filing

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual VAT return (Form 102) and final periodic VAT reconciliation
